edge_explainer: The screen ranked AEP on '6.1x EBIT, 27% of cap in net cash, +98% off the low'. Two of those three are wrong in a way no balance-sheet screen can see, and the third is right for the wrong reason. (1) COMMODITY FRAME REFUTES THE COMMODITY STORY: over the window in which AEP rose 196%, CPO rose 25% and the median listed palm peer rose 44%; over the 12 months in which AEP rose 90%, CPO rose 8% and peers 24%. Roughly 150pp of the move is idiosyncratic multiple. (2) THE CAUSE IS GOVERNANCE, NOT PALM: the controlling shareholder (Madam Lim Siew Kim, whose 52.6% Genton stake is in probate) died, and the company then re-based its dividend from a 15.0c FY23 final to 51.0c FY24 to 81.0c FY25, ran two buybacks, split the stock 10-for-1, rebranded, spent $171m of its hoard on acquisitions and put its Kalimantan arm up for an IDX IPO. The market priced a stake that became mobile. That re-rate cannot repeat: P/B went 0.55x -> 1.54x and EV/planted hectare ($10,223) now equals the $10,714/ha AEP itself paid for Pinago in May 2026 - the company printed its own fair-value comp. (3) THE NET CASH IS 83% SPENT: $232.3m at 31-Dec-25 less Pinago $162m, the Pinago MTO $3m, PT JJU $9m, the $16.8m final dividend paid 30-Jul-26 and $2.4m of buybacks = $193.2m consumed after the balance-sheet date, leaving pro-forma 7-10% of cap, not 27%. (Separately the screen's cash included $22.0m of 'Investments' the company excludes from its own net-cash statement.) (4) THE ESTATE IS UNDER-REPLANTED: no hectares-by-age table exists anywhere in the annual report - only an undefined 'Old 22% / Prime 38% / Young 26% / Immature 14%' donut - but the arithmetic is unambiguous. Steady state on 64,982 planted ha at a 25-year cycle is 2,599 ha/yr; realised is 1,625 ha/yr over four years (63%) and the stated 2026-2030 programme is 2,000 ha/yr (77%). Mature area already fell 1.7% in 2025, own FFB fell 2.7% in the five months to May-2026, external FFB purchased exceeded own production for the first time in 2025, and the Malaysian estate averages over 25 years at a 4.8 mt/ha yield against a group 19.2. Growth is being bought, not grown. (5) THE COMMODITY IS AT A 20-YEAR 90TH PERCENTILE ($1,109/mt vs a $767 20-yr median). You would be buying peak input on a tripled multiple with the cash cushion gone. (6) ANTI-MASKING / CLEAN FINDINGS, stated because absence of masking is itself information: capital commitments are $0.878m contracted (the THX test passes cleanly); there are no borrowings at all; both 2026 acquisitions are arm's-length third-party (Pinago from IDX-listed shareholders, PT JJU from listed CBIP), neither related-party; current Lim-family dealing is a $178,192 office lease. The historic related-party noise is historic. (7) ONE REVIEW-FLAG: the 20-May-26 RNS says the Indonesian export changes have no 'direct impact' because AEP sells only domestically - true - while the indirect channel it waves at is the dominant one. AEP's own two disclosed prices give a 25.9% wedge between CIF Rotterdam $1,151/mt and its realised ex-mill $853/mt, set largely by Indonesian duty and levy; each 1pp of that wedge is $4.9m, 4.4% of FY25 EBIT. The CEO cites B50 biodiesel demand as a price support without noting that the same programme is funded by the export levy that widens the wedge. One-sided emphasis, not misstatement - both numbers are printed in the same report. NET: fairly valued at E[FV] 170p vs 177p live. Not a trap and not a bargain; quality at its own history's PREMIUM, which is the wrong side of this lane's frame.
